results.title: TOC rising at point of use
results.text: A slow, steady rise in total organic carbon (TOC) at the point of use, with the upstream EDI outlet TOC rising in step, points to the organic-oxidation stage. Check the UV-185nm lamp intensity trend and the lamp runtime against its rated life before looking at downstream causes. If the EDI outlet TOC is normal while only the point-of-use analyzer rises, suspect the analyzer.

results.title: AMC rising in a process bay
results.text: Compare AMC at the make-up air inlet with AMC in the bay. If the inlet is steady while the bay rises, the chemical filtration stage is the likely source.

results.title: UV-185nm lamp ageing
results.text: UV lamp output falls as running hours accumulate. When lamp hours exceed the rated life, oxidation of organics becomes incomplete and TOC drifts upward, often with a falling UV intensity reading. Corrective action: plan lamp replacement, verify intensity after replacement, and re-measure TOC after the loop has flushed.

report.narrative: An investigation was conducted regarding the TOC excursion at point of use tag UPW_B_TOC_POU, which reached a measured level of 2.9891 ppb against a limit of 1.0 ppb. Sensor window data from E2 shows a sharp upward trend starting from 0.7428 ppb up to 2.9891 ppb over the last 120 minutes, with a rate of change slope of 1.1548 ppb per hour as indicated in E3. Upstream analysis via E12 demonstrates that the TOC at the EDI outlet (UPW_B_TOC_EDI) rose in lockstep from 0.6753 to 2.4762 ppb, ruling out a localized point-of-use analyzer sensor drift since both the process point and upstream stage reflect the elevation. Furthermore, evaluation of the UV-185nm lamp intensity sensor UPW_B_UV_INT via E9 reveals a significant drop from 81.0527 down to 66.2368 percent during the same 120-minute window, correlating directly with the rise in TOC. Knowledge base guidance UPW-01 and UPW-02 confirm that concurrent TOC increases at the EDI outlet and falling UV-185nm intensity point to organic-oxidation stage failure due to UV lamp decay. Calibration for the analyzer is confirmed valid under E1.
recommended_actions: It is recommended that a qualified engineer review the UV-185nm lamp status and schedule lamp replacement for asset UV_B.
It is recommended that a qualified engineer verify UV intensity readings and re-measure loop TOC after lamp replacement and system flushing.
It is recommended that a qualified engineer inspect upstream EDI performance parameters on asset EDI_B to ensure complete organic oxidation.
